message.content:
I am speech: breath shaped into sound, thought made audible.

I begin as an intention—before words—then I take form: vowels opened, consonants struck, rhythm and pause giving me meaning. I ride pitch and volume; I can soothe, persuade, teach, warn, confess, command.

I live in time. I vanish as I arrive, leaving echoes in air and in memory. I depend on a mouth, a throat, a tongue; I depend on an ear willing to receive me. I can be fluent or falter, honest or rehearsed, gentle or cutting.

I am not just what is said, but how: the tremor, the laughter, the silence between phrases. I can build bonds, start wars, make vows, tell stories, name things into being.

Speak, and I exist. Stop, and I am gone.
